rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Managing change requests**

I need to handle a legacy change request carefully while ensuring it links to the new system. It’s important to copy the incident details over, create references to both IDs, and update the legacy ticket with the new incident ID. I’ll also need to remind the team to avoid closing the legacy incident. For the action items: create the new incident, update the legacy ticket, leave the request in legacy, link if possible, and escalate issues internally.
rounds.response: Move the incident portion of mixed tickets into the new workflow by Fri 12:00; the change request may remain in the legacy tool until it is completed. For each mixed ticket, create a new incident record in the new system copying all incident details and include the legacy change ID in a dedicated reference field. In the legacy ticket add an explicit note “Incident migrated to new system — new ID: [ID]” and update the legacy incident-related status to “migrated” (or the nearest equivalent) so the team does not duplicate work. Maintain bi-directional links or clear cross-references and record the next action owner on both records to preserve continuity during handover. If you expect any queues cannot meet Fri 12:00, send me the queue names and specific operational risks now so I can consolidate for the VP’s 16:00 deadline tomorrow.

rounds.consequence: The line manager applies your guidance to brief the shift team and starts compiling a list of mixed tickets marked as either split or escalated. No conflicting instructions emerge from other sources, and migration support acknowledges receipt of a few escalated ticket IDs without asking you to change your approach.

rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Updating queue handling notes**

I've got four sentences here, but I think it might be helpful to mention updating the queue handling notes. I’ll say something like, "Update queue handling notes accordingly," though it feels a bit redundant. I want to keep it concise, under five sentences if possible, focusing on concrete actions or communications. I’ll make sure to use neutral language and only mention "create new incident record" when necessary. Alright, it’s time to write the final version!
rounds.response: Only incident records that remain "open" (i.e., require further incident work) must be migrated to the new system by Fri 12:00; resolved/closed incident records that require no further incident action may remain in the legacy tool. If the resolved incident could be reopened or if any incident-related activity is still expected while the change continues, treat it as open and create the incident in the new system by Fri 12:00. For resolved incidents left in legacy, add a clear note on the legacy change record: "Incident resolved pre-cutover — legacy incident ID: [ID]; no incident migration required," and include that legacy incident ID in any change-related references so traceability is preserved. If you are unsure about a specific ticket, tag it with the ticket ID and a one-line reason and route it to the Line Manager now for escalation before the next handover.
